name: Model Tier Chooser
description: Picks, for each of the four model tiers (fast, balanced, quality, best), the provider, model and reasoning effort that is the cheapest and fastest of the arms at least as good as the tier's held default on public evaluations (capability only for best); which tier each call role uses is decided by the role-tier metric (role_tiers.csv over role_tier_metrics.csv): the lowest tier unless the next tier up shows a significant gain on the public evaluations that speak to the role's kind of call, with the owner's hard constraints applied after.
purpose: Pick, for each model tier, the model that best fits what the tier is for, by that tier's own metric.
approach: Keep arms with current public numbers, a list price and a published speed that reach the tier's anchored minimums (the held default's scores less a tolerance; tier_metrics.csv over registry/tier_public_scores.csv and tier_prices.csv), then score cost and speed with a small capability bonus; a missing number means not eligible; an arm at an effort the caller does not apply is not eligible; best uses capability alone.
out_of_scope: Calling the model (the Vendor Model Caller does that) and the wording of the question (each part does that).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-model-tier-chooser has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: The chosen model per tier is the top of that tier's public metric, with its score breakdown, runner-up and evidence mark (direct or proxy). Every row of the role-tier table names the public evaluations, the two tiers' scores, the gap against the threshold, the date and whether the evidence is direct or proxy; none says unmeasured.
parameters: bars: optional keyword arguments that set the quality bars.
inputs: tiers (tier name to candidate arms with cases run, cases passed and tokens), prices (rows from the price file), optional credits and defaults.
outputs: A mapping from each tier to the chosen provider, model and effort, with the reason, the stage, the evidence mark and the score breakdown.
usage_notes: The default arm needs nothing from the consumer.
